topic: Feedback-core exact-risk certification for weighted random isolation. Revive banked parent exp_awri_mixture_minimax_certificate with a different mathematical angle: given its fixed WRI/RDIM network-design model and a supplied size-k feedback vertex set of the conflict graph, prove an evaluated cutoff-forest moment algebra that computes every one/two-tagged greedy-isolated-set count polynomial and dense rational RDIM risk matrix in L n^2 2^{O(k log(k+1))} poly(n,b,lambda) bit operations, with no (nb)^k table or unevaluated integration gate. Use the derived 3^k core inclusion-exclusion reduction, complete vertex-cover oracle, and ordered-ratio nested-moment recurrence as traction; close heterogeneous forest branching, moving boundary integration, all tags, and intermediate bit height. Then return a rational epsilon-minimax primal-dual certificate for the finite rule library; omit the parent's unsupported exact algebraic optimizer. Consumer: exact AWRI rule selection for a rural-China insurance-diffusion follow-up after measuring the conflict graph's feedback number. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A three-state cutoff-forest reduction and exact core inclusion-exclusion identity were derived; vertex-cover cores are FPT, and a directed-realizable feedback-k family with binomial dense support has an O(k! k m^2) nested-ratio evaluation. Exact checks matched all 44 C6 tag polynomials, 288 risk entries, 384 vertex-cover queries, six repeated-star cases, and three heterogeneous cases. Relative core order and scalar activation counts both failed, while no prior-art collision or universal obstruction was found. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove an evaluated moment representation for heterogeneous cutoff-forest messages that preserves future core-priority exponent profiles and closes under branching, component products, moving-endpoint integration, and tagged coefficient extraction in true FPT bit complexity. EARLY KILL TEST: On heterogeneous replicated-star integrals with k<=3, m<=2, and branch weights in {1,2}, match all tags and the private-leaf encoding to exact residual enumeration and prove symbolic arbitrary-k,m complexity; if closure still indexes k degree totals or profile-count vectors with an n-dependent exponent, stop and pivot before general forest or SDP work. source_refs.claim: WRI uses heterogeneous Beta priorities, and its paper treats analytical evaluation of the MSE surrogate as complicated and instead estimates it by simulation.
source_refs.author: Changhao Shi, Haoyu Yang, Yichen Qin, Yang Li

source_refs.claim: Random sequential adsorption gives a continuous-time random-greedy independent-set recursion on regular tree-like graphs and restricted cyclic families, not heterogeneous tagged finite-graph moments.
source_refs.author: Nicholas Pippenger

source_refs.claim: Bounded-treewidth dynamic programming can compute static independent-set counts of every size, but it does not incorporate probabilities induced by heterogeneous greedy priority orders.
source_refs.author: Pengfei Wan, Jianhua Tu, Shenggui Zhang, Binlong Li

open_problems.why_unsolved: The parent closes only unconditional rooted-forest messages. Conditioning on a feedback core introduces heterogeneous numerical cutoffs determined by future core priorities: child messages must multiply across branches and components, survive moving-endpoint integration, and retain enough information for all tagged coefficients. Scalar occupation recursions from random sequential adsorption and static independent-set dynamic programs do not provide this closure. Direct multivariate priority-exponent tables have an n-dependent exponent, while the supplied three-state reduction, core inclusion-exclusion identity, and repeated-star checks remain presolve evidence requiring theorem-level validation and a polynomial intermediate-bit-height argument.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A correctness-and-bit-complexity theorem that first validates the proposed three-state cutoff messages and 3^k core inclusion-exclusion identity, then gives an evaluated representation closed under heterogeneous branching, component products, moving-boundary integration, and tagged extraction in L n^2 2^{O(k log(k+1))} poly(n,b,lambda) bit operations.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its progression from interference-safe isolation through representativeness and random sample-size risk to the need for choosing priority rules.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Network interference invalidates ordinary assignment -> weighted random isolation creates compatible focal units but makes exact risk analytically difficult -> feedback-small conflict graphs may permit exact certified rule selection

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the time-indexed tree occupation recursion and its proof by conditioning on accepted priorities, replacing scalar occupation messages by boundary-conditioned tagged moments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Random sequential adsorption is the unweighted random-order greedy independent-set mechanism; the proposed resolution needs its finite, weighted, core-conditioned analogue.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the distributional bonus recursion for randomized greedy selection and its rooted-subtree independence argument to heterogeneous moving cutoffs.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It demonstrates recursive control of weighted greedy decisions on trees, the structural step that must be strengthened to preserve future core-priority profiles.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the RDIM risk decomposition into balance and inverse-isolated-sample-size moments, then express those moments through the tagged count polynomials.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It fixes the causal-design quantities the message algebra must compute, preventing substitution of an unrelated static independent-set count.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The closest proposed negative route imports hardness intuition from counting linear extensions, but a poset order constraint is not a WRI greedy-domination certificate. No source problem, domination gadget, exact coefficient-recovery identity, or proof that feedback vertex number grows only with the source parameter was supplied. The dense XP representation and the heterogeneous-profile obstruction therefore do not establish hardness, leaving the positive feedback-core algorithm logically possible.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A parameter-preserving parsimonious or FPT Turing reduction whose output conflict graph has feedback vertex number f(k), whose positive weights have polynomial encoding length, and whose single specified tagged coefficient recovers the source count, thereby establishing #W[1]-hardness.

The web literature supports mixed minimax experimental designs and conflict-graph risk comparisons, but does not provide the required end-to-end rational certificate for this finite WRI library and graph-ellipsoid adversary. open_problems.open_problem: Under sequences of bounded-feedback conflict graphs, does graph-only selection from a finite WRI rule library preserve a uniformly valid studentized design-based central limit theorem for RDIM despite the random greedy support and reciprocal arm counts?

source_refs.excerpt: no studentized RDIM limit law is supplied
WRI first generates a random greedy support whose membership can depend on distant priority changes

open_problems.why_unsolved: Conditioning on the isolated set yields an ordinary balanced focal assignment but does not justify unconditioning: the support is a global function of weighted priorities, may be compositionally unrepresentative, and introduces random reciprocal denominators. A bounded feedback core suggests conditioning on finitely many core states and proving forest stabilization componentwise, but the prior proposal supplies neither a localization bound for distant priority changes nor uniform denominator control after graph-only rule selection.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sufficient-condition theorem giving a uniform conditional-to-unconditional CLT and a consistent design-based studentizer for the selected RDIM rule, with explicit feedback-core growth, component-size, influence, and isolated-count nondegeneracy conditions.

writing_exemplar.why: Extend its WRI/RDIM consistency motivation into a precise finite-population inference question while retaining its estimator and graph-only rule-selection setting.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: WRI creates exposure-compatible focal samples -> RDIM estimates the universal-treatment contrast using random support and denominators -> deployment requires studentized design-based inference after graph-only rule selection

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt exposure-probability variance accounting and design-based asymptotic-normality arguments after establishing feedback-core localization and denominator stabilization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies general-interference design-based inference machinery; the missing step is to make WRI's generated support satisfy analogous regularity conditions.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt local-limit analysis of random-greedy maximal independent sets to control how forest neighborhoods determine inclusion after conditioning on a small feedback core.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The WRI support is the same random-greedy combinatorial object, and a CLT first needs quantitative localization of its inclusion indicators.

literature_map:
Shi, Yang, Qin, and Li (2024, arXiv:2408.15670) introduce Beta-priority WRI and RDIM, explicitly replacing analytically complicated MSE evaluation by simulation.
Ugander and Yin (2023, JCI, arXiv:2009.02297) randomize graph clustering and need pair co-exposure probabilities for exact HT variance, estimating them by Monte Carlo.
Ugander, Karrer, Backstrom, and Kleinberg (2013, KDD, arXiv:1305.6979) show exact exposure-probability computation for fixed graph-cluster randomization, an important exact-but-less-randomized baseline.
Cai, Zhang, and Airoldi (2024, ICLR, arXiv:2312.04026) use independent sets to control treatment and spillover exposures, but do not evaluate the WRI output law.
Aronow and Samii (2017, AOAS, DOI 10.1214/16-AOAS1005) make marginal and joint exposure probabilities the core inputs to design-based point and variance estimation.
Leung (2022, Econometrica, arXiv:1911.07085) supplies asymptotic inference under approximate neighborhood interference rather than finite-instance exact design risk.
Kandiros, Pipis, Daskalakis, and Harshaw (2024, arXiv:2411.10908) make the conflict graph a design object and derive spectral risk rates and conservative inference.
Kandiros, Harshaw, and Sävje (2026, arXiv:2608.04909) show minimax risk is determined by the conflict graph but leave its exact relationship complicated and potentially computationally hard.
Pippenger (1989, SIAM JDM, DOI 10.1137/0402034) gives dynamic occupation recursions for uniform random sequential adsorption on tree-like graphs.
Gamarnik and Goldberg (2010, CPC, arXiv:0807.1277) analyze weighted random greedy independent sets by subtree distributional recursions, but for limiting expectations.
Krivelevich, Mészáros, Michaeli, and Shikhelman (2024, RSA, arXiv:1907.07216) develop local-limit random-greedy MIS recursions and tree results, not finite heterogeneous tagged moments.
Wan, Tu, Zhang, and Li (2018, AMC, DOI 10.1016/j.amc.2018.03.017) compute all-size independent-set polynomials on bounded-treewidth graphs, but for static set weights rather than greedy-order probabilities.
Borie, Parker, and Tovey (1992, Algorithmica, DOI 10.1007/BF01758777) provide the finite-state tree-decomposition DP paradigm; its unit-cost/static-state framework does not settle moving-cutoff rational bit complexity.
Cygan, Pilipczuk, Pilipczuk, and Wojtaszczyk (2011, ICALP, arXiv:1004.2972) establish the relevant 2^{O(k log k)} FVS-style parameterized scale.
Kallus (2021, JRSSB, DOI 10.1111/rssb.12412), Tardos (1986, Operations Research), and Dadush-Vegh-Zambelli (2022, SODA) jointly support mixed minimax design plus exact rational primal-dual certification; Cai-de Janvry-Sadoulet (2015, AEJ Applied, DOI 10.1257/app.20130442) supplies the rural-China insurance-diffusion destination.
